CE1.label: Resolution difficulty

CE1.1.label: Not resolved on first contact
CE1.1.description: Customer had to contact support more than once to resolve the same issue.

CE1.2.label: Multiple steps required for simple issue
CE1.2.description: An issue that should have been straightforward required excessive steps or approvals.

CE1.3.label: Partial or incomplete resolution
CE1.3.description: The resolution provided only addressed part of the customer's issue, leaving other aspects unresolved.

CE1.4.label: Resolution delayed beyond expectation
CE1.4.description: Resolution took significantly longer than the customer expected or was promised.

CE1.5.label: Other resolution difficulty
CE1.5.description: A resolution difficulty that does not fit another sub-category.

CE1.description: The customer had to work hard to achieve resolution: the issue was complex, required multiple steps, or was not resolved on the first attempt.

CE2.label: Process burden

CE2.1.label: Excessive information or documentation required
CE2.1.description: Customer was asked to provide more information, documents, or verification than seemed necessary.

CE2.2.label: Repetitive identity verification
CE2.2.description: Customer had to verify their identity or repeat account details multiple times in the same interaction.

CE2.3.label: Required to contact multiple departments
CE2.3.description: Customer was passed between teams or departments and had to re-explain their issue.

CE2.4.label: Complex or non-intuitive self-service process
CE2.4.description: The self-service option available required too much effort or knowledge to complete.

CE2.5.label: Other process burden
CE2.5.description: A process burden that does not fit another sub-category.

CE2.description: The company's processes, policies, or procedures created unnecessary effort for the customer.

CE3.label: Communication friction

CE3.1.label: Unclear or confusing guidance from agent
CE3.1.description: Instructions provided by the agent were unclear, ambiguous, or hard to follow.

CE3.2.label: Inconsistent information across contacts
CE3.2.description: Customer received different answers from different agents about the same question.

CE3.3.label: Use of unexplained technical jargon
CE3.3.description: Agent used technical terms or acronyms the customer did not understand, requiring clarification.

CE3.4.label: Insufficient proactive communication
CE3.4.description: Customer had to ask for updates rather than being proactively informed of progress or status.

CE3.5.label: Other communication friction
CE3.5.description: A communication friction point that does not fit another sub-category.

CE3.description: Friction caused by how information was communicated: clarity, consistency, or availability of guidance.

CE4.label: Channel and access friction

CE4.1.label: Excessive wait time or hold time
CE4.1.description: Customer experienced significant wait times to reach an agent or receive a response.

CE4.2.label: Forced to use non-preferred channel
CE4.2.description: Customer was required to switch to a channel they did not prefer (e.g. phone when email was preferred).

CE4.3.label: No adequate self-service option
CE4.3.description: Self-service was not available for a task that should be achievable without agent involvement.

CE4.4.label: Difficult or ineffective IVR or chatbot
CE4.4.description: Automated phone system or chatbot could not route or handle the customer's request.

CE4.5.label: Other channel friction
CE4.5.description: A channel or access friction issue that does not fit another sub-category.

CE4.description: Friction caused by the support channels available: wait times, forced channel switches, or inability to use the customer's preferred channel.

CE5.label: Information and knowledge gaps

CE5.1.label: Documentation insufficient or missing
CE5.1.description: Help articles, FAQs, or user guides did not cover the customer's scenario.

CE5.2.label: Conflicting information between channels
CE5.2.description: Customer found different answers in the help centre vs. what the agent told them, or between different help articles.

CE5.3.label: Information not available in preferred language
CE5.3.description: Documentation or support was not available in the customer's language.

CE5.4.label: Other information gap
CE5.4.description: An information gap that does not fit another sub-category.

CE5.description: Customer struggled due to insufficient, hard-to-find, or incorrect product information.

CE6.label: Repeat contact and follow-up burden

CE6.1.label: Had to chase for promised follow-up
CE6.1.description: Agent committed to a follow-up action but the customer had to initiate contact again to prompt it.

CE6.2.label: Case closed prematurely
CE6.2.description: Support ticket or case was closed before the issue was resolved, requiring the customer to reopen or create a new contact.

CE6.3.label: Had to re-explain issue to new agent
CE6.3.description: Customer was transferred or had to contact again and repeat the full context to a new agent.

CE6.4.label: Other repeat contact burden
CE6.4.description: A repeat contact or follow-up burden that does not fit another sub-category.

CE6.description: Customer had to make multiple contacts, chase for updates, or re-engage because follow-up actions were not completed as promised.

CE7.label: Emotional labour

CE7.1.label: Had to argue or advocate for resolution
CE7.1.description: Customer felt they were not believed or had to push back repeatedly before the agent acted on their request.

CE7.2.label: Felt dismissed or not taken seriously
CE7.2.description: Customer expressed that their issue was minimised, dismissed, or not treated as valid.

CE7.3.label: Emotional distress during interaction
CE7.3.description: Customer expressed significant distress, anxiety, or upset during the interaction beyond normal frustration.

CE7.4.label: Other emotional burden
CE7.4.description: An emotional burden that does not fit another sub-category.

CE7.description: The customer experienced significant emotional burden during the interaction: had to advocate, argue, or manage their own emotions to achieve resolution.
